C0.quote: the effect of weighing voters according to their estimated fault
C0.note: Borderline: general-domain truth discovery for crowdsourcing labels, but the ranking part aggregates workers' rankings with (weighted) voting rules and proves weighted Kemeny is the MLE (epistemic voting). ELIG and INELIG fit about equally well, so ELIG (listed first) is chosen per the doubt rule.

C1.loc: Introduction, Contribution and paper structure; Sec. 3; Sec. 4; Sec. 5
C1.quote: we prove a formal version of the Anna Karenina principle
C1.note: OT = statistical/epistemic estimation results (Anna Karenina theorem and corollaries on expected average distance vs. competence; weighted Kemeny as MLE, Theorem 7). AL = the P-TD aggregation algorithm. SI = synthetic Mallows datasets. EM = real crowdsourcing datasets (DOTS, PUZZ, BUILD).

C2.1.value: report (of worker i); dataset S; answers/labels; rankings
C2.1.quote: Input: Dataset S ∈ L(k)n , voting rule r.

C2.2.quote: the set of all permutations over a set of candidates C
C2.2.note: Voting rules take strict rankings (permutations). OTH: in the general truth-discovery framework, aggregation also takes binary-vector and real-valued labels, and the weighted rules additionally take worker weights w.

C2.3.quote: The type ti of a worker determines her distribution of answers.
C2.3.note: Workers have types/fault levels (noise parameters) attributed independently of their reports; no preferences are attributed.

C2.4.quote: the report of worker i is a random variable si sampled from
C2.4.note: The held attribute (type t_i / fault f_i) has separate notation from the submitted report s_i, which is a noisy sample from Y(z, t_i).

C3.1.quote: Future work will consider how to identify and/or mitigate
C3.1.note: All reports are generated by the noise model; strategic workers are mentioned only as a shortcoming and future work.

C3.2.loc: Checked: Abstract, Sec. 1 Introduction, Sec. 2 Preliminaries, Sec. 3, Sec. 4, Sec. 5, Sec. 6 Conclusion
C3.2.note: Reports are described as sampled from a noise model given type and ground truth; no statement that workers truthfully submit what they hold/observe.

C4.1.note: No utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost, distortion or intensity notion is used for voters; evaluation is by error (distance to ground truth) and worker fault/competence.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' or an equivalent is not used.

C5.1.quote: The error of every algorithm is the distance (as specified above) to
C5.1.note: Outcomes are evaluated by accuracy (distance to the ground truth), not by welfare, efficiency, satisfaction, representation, proportionality or distortion.

VOT.quote_behav: Workers each report their answers S, which depend on the ground truth
VOT.note: Workers (voters) submit reports drawn from a noise model (Mallows / Condorcet noise) determined by type and ground truth; info is NA because behaviour is non-strategic.

ORG.note: The voting rule is fixed and treated as part of the input; no organiser takes an action in the model.

DES.note: The paper proposes an algorithm but does not model a designer agent's choice or objective.

C9.2.quote: a group of workers that submit similar labels (e.g. by acting strategically)
C9.2.note: The practical claims rest largely on empirical accuracy against ground truth; the needed assumption that workers report non-strategically (noise-model reports, no colluding groups) is stated in the model and explicitly acknowledged as a limitation in the conclusion.
